content: Large plaque parapsoriasis, also referred to as parapsoriasis en plaques, is a dermatological condition characterized by skin lesions. These lesions are typically included within the broader classification of parapsoriasis. The plaques are generally 10 centimeters or larger in diameter. They may present as very thin plaques that are either asymptomatic or mildly pruritic (itchy). Large plaque parapsoriasis is frequently associated with retiform parapsoriasis and may be accompanied by poikiloderma vasculare atrophicans, a condition marked by skin atrophy, pigmentation changes, and telangiectasia. In rare cases, large plaque parapsoriasis can serve as a precursor to cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, a type of skin lymphoma. Diagnosis The diagnosis of large plaque parapsoriasis is primarily clinical, based on the physical examination of the skin. The condition is often documented and studied using dermatological atlases for reference and comparison. Treatment The primary treatment for parapsoriasis involves light therapy, specifically PUVA therapy (psoralen combined with ultraviolet A) or UVB therapy. These treatments may be used in conjunction with topical corticosteroids to manage the condition. Large plaque parapsoriasis is typically a chronic condition that requires long-term management and treatment to control symptoms and prevent progression.
